NAV1 strengthened: the phone bar WRAPPER must not scroll either (PR #32 stopgap removed for real)
runs.note: R011 claimed the horizontal-scroll stopgap was gone. It was gone from .nav but still on the .side wrapper, and NAV1 only measured .nav — so the claim was true of the guard and false of the app. Wrapper rule removed; NAV1 now asserts both the wrapper's scrollWidth and its computed overflow-x, and a new NAV1 mutation restores the stopgap to prove the guard sees it.

runs.trigger: Levi's phone screenshot: body text clipped mid-sentence and the bar cut off — the five-slot bar had NEVER applied
runs.note: R012 was WRONG about the phone. Three separate faults, none of which any guard could see. (1) `.ol2.on{grid-template-columns:1fr}` — 1fr is minmax(auto,1fr) and its auto minimum is min-content, so the single column resolved to ~590px inside a 390px viewport and .ol2's position:fixed;inset:0 CLIPPED the overflow, which is why body text was cut mid-sentence while documentElement.scrollWidth stayed clean. (2) The mobile bar rules were written as `.nav a` (0,1,1) against a base rule of `.ol2 .nav a` (0,2,1) — they LOST on specificity, so flex:1 1 0 never applied and the five slots never existed. (3) PR #32's real stopgap was a LATER equal-specificity block (flex:0 0 auto + white-space:nowrap) that I never found; in R012 I removed only overflow-x:auto, which turned a swipeable bar into an unreachable one. NAV1 measured nav.scrollWidth-nav.clientWidth — the bar against ITSELF — which reports zero for an oversized bar hanging off the screen. It now measures every slot's rect against the viewport, forces the 5th slot visible (the fixture has 0 needs-review so it never rendered), and fails on clipped labels. MOB1 is new and checks the WHOLE page for elements past the right edge.

runs.trigger: app_events had 0 rows; diagnosing whether the event layer was broken or merely unused
runs.note: VERDICT: the emitter was never broken. Proven against PRODUCTION, not a stub — a raw insert from Levi's signed-in browser returned 201, and window.lpEvent('diag.viafn') wrote a real row. RLS, both CHECK constraints, and the _lpSb/_lpWs/_lpUser globals were all correct. The zero rows meant nobody had performed an instrumented action on a page loaded after the layer deployed (a tab open since before the deploy runs the old code). The REAL defect was that this was unanswerable without a database probe: lpEvent swallowed every outcome, so success, RLS denial, network failure and signed-out skip all looked identical from outside — nothing. Fixed by making the layer falsifiable: _lpEvStats counts sent/failed/skipped and keeps the last error, failures reach console.warn, an app.loaded heartbeat fires once per signed-in load so an empty table can ONLY mean broken, and Settings states the recording state in words. EV4/EV5/EV6 added and mutation-proven. AK4 was rewritten too: it counted app_events inserts and broke the moment the heartbeat was added — a guard that counts is a guard that fails for the wrong reason, so it now asserts the event by NAME. Two diagnostic rows (diag.probe, diag.viafn) are permanent in app_events: the table has no delete policy by design. They are honestly named and harmless.

runs.trigger: Roadmap items 3-5: email deliverables, purchase decision briefs, classifier rebuilt from the typed portfolio
runs.note: EMAIL (F2b): the largest typed bucket, 12 cards. api/send.js already existed and was never reachable from a card. lpEmailParse pulls To/Subject/Body out of the draft; a bare name like 'To: Chad' is REFUSED as an address rather than guessed at, send is two-step and the confirm names the recipient, and an unverified sending domain is reported as a setup problem instead of a generic failure. EM1/EM2/EM3. PURCHASE (F2c): 8 cards, the garage-lightbulbs case. No payment path — the standing rule is intact and PU2 asserts it. The load-bearing constraint is prices: this project has a fabrication precedent, so a price is only presented as real when its row carries a source URL; everything else is struck through and marked UNSOURCED with a warning. The PARSER enforces it — Wingman is not trusted to be honest about its own sourcing. PU1/PU2. CLASSIFIER: the problem was the TYPE LIST, not the regexes. Of 48 unplaceable cards, 14 were configuring another system, 8 access/account admin, 7 reviews, 4 training. `setup` is now the LARGEST bucket in the whole portfolio — bigger than email — and had no name at all. Added setup, review, admin, learning; habits and chores now abstain by design. Measured against the REAL 48: 0/48 → 37/48, and 6 of the 11 remaining are habits/chores that should abstain, so 37 of 42 real asset cards (88%). CL1's fixtures are production titles, not invented ones. One judgement call: 'Give me a list of all trailers FOR SALE' matched purchase before research. An explicit request for a list is research even when the subject is a purchase, so list/search intent is now probed first. CONFIRM: all 37 typed cards were still marked inferred days after the backfill because confirming meant re-picking from the dropdown. The GUESS chip is now a one-tap confirm. CL2.

runs.trigger: F15 member IDs (decision #6, pulled forward into Stage 1)
runs.note: Production sized the problem before anything was built: workspace_members holds exactly TWO people (Levi, Zoe) while cards assign work to FOUR — Chad (2 cards) and Jason (1) have no account at all. Team Workload was rendering seven people as though all were on the team; three of them cannot sign in, cannot see the work, and will never receive a notification. Design: ids ride ALONGSIDE names, names are NOT removed. 85 cards depend on the name strings and a big-bang migration with no rollback is how data gets lost. newItemBase stamps assigneeIds at creation, lpBackfillMemberIds fills existing cards once the roster loads, and a card naming a non-member is left exactly as it is — inventing an id for someone with no account would paper over the gap this exists to surface. The workload now marks them NO ACCOUNT and says in words what that costs. Two deliberate subtleties, both mutation-proven: name matching is trim/case-insensitive, and an unloaded roster returns 'unknown' rather than 'unlinked' — painting 'no account' across the whole crew because a fetch has not returned yet is worse than saying nothing.

runs.trigger: Decision #7: capture interview. Task-detail relayout checked against production first and found already shipped.
runs.note: DETAIL RELAYOUT: NOT rebuilt. Levi's complaint ('I cannot see all of the information') predated the tab strip and notes auto-grow. Checked production directly before touching anything: 5 tabs render and are visible, notes are 105px and not scrollable, the pane is 1.4 screens. Rebuilding what is already fixed would have been busywork; his judgement on the current build is what settles it. A LOCAL-HARNESS TRAP worth knowing: in the signed-out fixture, opening a card renders the detail and then hides it ~570ms later, so #ol2Review ends up display:none. This does NOT happen on production (verified in Levi's signed-in browser: the pane opens and stays). Any future guard that drives the detail pane in the local harness will pass or fail for the wrong reason — check production before believing it. CAPTURE INTERVIEW: built to Levi's own words. Questions are computed from what the parse MISSED, not asked of a model — instant, works offline, and cannot ask about a detail the person already gave. Asking 'when is this due?' about a card that says 'due Friday' is how an interview becomes a tax. The definition-of-done question is marked MATTERS MOST because 41% deliverable coverage is the reason drafts kept landing as the easy 20%. His rule applied literally: a DO-IT card with no definition of done parks in Waiting on Levi rather than drafting against a guess — and a parked card no longer emits task.routed, so the routed count cannot lie. Track-it cards never park; that is his own work. CI3 exists because I INTRODUCED a bug building this: the taller preview pushed Confirm off the bottom of a phone. The button was in the DOM, matched a selector, and could not be clicked. Three existing guards (C1, EV3, AT1) went red and caught it. 'Present in the DOM' is not 'reachable by a thumb'.

runs.trigger: Decision #8 realtime Ask + F3 knowledge-base rewrite
runs.note:
FIRST FULLY GREEN RUN. 71/71, zero failures, zero errors. X34A/X34B had been the only two red checks since the suite was rebuilt on Aug 22.
REALTIME: the supabase_realtime publication contained NO TABLES, so a subscription would have sat silent forever and looked like working code. Migration ask_turns_realtime adds the table; RLS still scopes delivery to user_id = auth.uid(), so one person's conversation cannot reach another's socket, and REPLICA IDENTITY stays DEFAULT rather than putting every turn's text in the WAL. Two things the client must get right and both are mutation-proven: your own insert echoes back down the socket and must not double-post, and a realtime failure must not take the Ask panel down — the pull-on-open path is untouched. The label only says 'Live' when a channel is actually open.
DOCS: rewritten from scratch against the app as it now is. The old set was Aug 17 and described three surfaces that no longer exist (My Day, My Week, Libraries) while never naming Today.
X34C is new and is the important one: X34A hard-codes the five destinations in the SUITE, so it can only ever be as current as the test file — retire a surface and it keeps passing while the docs rot. X34C derives the nav from the running app and the claims from docs.json and checks them against EACH OTHER. It also asserts the docs state the standing limits (no buying, nothing sends without you, decks not generated) and derives the deck claim from LP_FILE_TYPES rather than trusting prose.

runs.trigger: Decisions #9 and #10: the AI grade and the confidence quiz — the last two roadmap items
runs.note: GRADE: usage 40 / momentum 35 / effectiveness 25, as agreed. The arithmetic matters less than the refusal: below 12 real events in 30 days it returns NO SCORE and says why. A grade drawn from an almost-empty events table is a confident number meaning nothing, and this project already lost a day to that class of mistake. GR1 mutation-proves the refusal AND that the diag.* rows left behind by that same investigation are excluded — otherwise the first grade Levi ever saw would have been inflated by my own debugging.\nMomentum is completions against creations, damped by how much is overdue RIGHT NOW, so a pile of late work cannot score well on flow alone. Effectiveness is approvals over drafts REVIEWED, not over drafts made — a draft nobody has looked at is not evidence of anything.\nQUIZ: 16 questions, pass at 70% inclusive (mutation-proven at the boundary — 'pass is 70' failing at exactly 70 would be a lie). Several questions are about the LIMITS: what Wingman will not do, why an unsourced price is struck through, why a deck cannot be generated. Knowing the limits is what makes delegation safe. A partly-filled sheet is refused rather than scored, because that percentage would measure how much was skipped rather than what is known.
